page: Microsoft Azure D2ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPSv5 server family. It is powered by an ARM64-based Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a dedicated frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance features 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs, meaning there is no hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest performance characteristics. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the average tier. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics show limitations. The multi-core stress-ng performance and Geekbench single-core scores fall into the weak category, while the Geekbench multi-core score and PassMark CPU score register in the poor tier. Memory bandwidth tests show 140.47 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 23.96 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations, achieve 2.74 million operations per second, which is classified as weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ps_v5 offers a low-cost entry point into ARM64 computing on Azure, utilizing dedicated physical cores rather than shared-core resources. This makes it a viable option for lightweight workloads that benefit from a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without requiring high-performance multi-threaded compute or high memory bandwidth. Suitable workloads include basic web serving, lightweight database operations, simple text processing, and development or testing environments optimized for the ARM architecture.
